mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) despite the rate increase, or the rate increase is not sustained for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 6% while PAYEMS rises by > 10,000 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) even when both proxies move in the predicted direction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating supply-side demand, which typically precedes equity market expansion and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO growth meeting or exceeding the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% in a month while output (GDPC1) remains flat, it suggests supply-side constraints that raise uncertainty and depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +0.5% and GDPC1 monthly change <= 0%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the 1-month unemployment rate (UNRATE) followed by a sustained rise in the 3-month personal income (not directly observable but proxy via labor proxies like PAYEMS) predicts a shift to a more expansionary monetary policy stance, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 5% and remains below for 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when labor indicators show expansion.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) without a corresponding decline in job openings (not directly observable) implies tight labor markets that raise wage growth expectations and drive equity valuations higher, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive despite rising PAYEMS momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 3% for two consecutive months is interpreted as a deepening supply-side recession, which typically precedes equity market corrections and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for 10 consecutive days, it indicates a high-interest environment that discourages risk-taking and suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when the FEDFUNDS condition is met.
